claim: The canary proof tool (tools/credentials/canary_proof.py, 1,834 lines, with the contained scan worker tools/credentials/canary_scan_worker.py, 2,114 lines) passed its synthetic acceptance on the workstation on 2026-10-01 on main with the K4 guard: its unit suite ran 143 tests, OK, with none skipped (including 12 cases that start transient systemd user scopes); its mutation runner killed 138 of 138 mutants by failures of their named permanent tests after 90 passing unmutated runs; and the credential, guard, Codex worker-lane and pre-commit suites ran 531 tests with one failure by design (the installed host copy of the guard). The tool plants a unique synthetic canary, lets named consumers use it through the key runner, and searches the named sinks with ripgrep in a worker that runs in a finite systemd user scope; its classifier refuses unless every required check has a fresh, complete result bound to the run. Reviews: a read-only GPT-6 verification found seven paths to a false clean verdict and four high findings, and an Opus build review found one blocking gap in the contract's acceptance cases; one repair round by a GPT-6 runtime worker fixed them, each with a permanent test and a mutant; an Opus re-check confirmed 37 of 42 dispositions and found one more false-clean path (a Git object store with no HEAD, refs or .git name, reached directly) and a record-validation defect, which one bounded fix round closed with tests and mutants. No end-to-end proof has run: it is the new distribution's acceptance after its guard install.
limitations: Synthetic acceptance only: every sink, canary, Git store, SQLite database and journal in these runs is a fixture the tests build under a temporary directory; no real consumer, transcript, log, journal or credential was used, and no proof claim is made before the end-to-end run.

Containment evidence is workstation scope enforcement: the real-scope classes start transient systemd user scopes on this host (12 cases, all passing); hosted CI runners skip them where no user scope exists.
Scanner: ripgrep 14.1.0 is the executed version; the runtime also accepts 15.2.0 on a source-reviewed output grammar that no run has executed.

Size: the implementation (3,948 coordinator and worker lines) and the permanent test file (3,632 lines) exceed the contract's ceilings (1,800 and 2,800); the coordinator accepted the deviation for the required coverage and containment logic, and the reviews' dead-code findings were removed.

Residuals from the Opus re-check, recorded in the decision record: a completed but too-early or stale final is labelled requested_incomplete; the WAL/SHM-without-valid-main guard, Walk.covered's exclusion, time, special-file and symlinked-parent branches, and several O12 changes have no test of their own; three mutants are missing (END count/aux, --text, a count-based Git reconcile); bind_scope's refusal paths and the real scope_populated parser are untested; the scan's exit code still comes from events it does not validate.
Evidence classes differ: the unit, mutation and suite runs were made by the coordinator on the final head outside any sandbox; the reviews are read-only cross-family reads, not proofs.
evidence_class: local integration (the tool's unit suite, mutation runner and the credential and guard suites on this host, run by the coordinator, including transient systemd user scopes) plus read-only cross-family reviews: a GPT-6 (gpt-6-astra, effort max) verification, an Opus build review and an Opus re-check
